summary: The article accurately reports on American Express's Q2 earnings, including revenue, billed business, and the market's reaction to rising costs.

claims.claim: American Express reported a 10% increase in quarterly revenue, reaching $19.6 billion.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm American Express's Q2 2026 revenue was $19.6 billion, a 10% increase year-over-year.

claims.claim: Total card spending, or billed business, grew 9% year-over-year to $455.8 billion on an FX-adjusted basis.
claims.note: Several sources confirm billed business grew 9% year-over-year to $455.8 billion on an FX-adjusted basis.

claims.claim: Despite robust earnings and a higher revenue outlook, American Express shares experienced a tumble.
claims.note: Numerous articles report that American Express shares fell despite strong earnings and a raised revenue outlook, due to concerns over rising costs.

claims.claim: The decline in share price was primarily attributed to concerns over rising costs impacting investor sentiment.
claims.note: Multiple sources explicitly state that rising costs and expenses were the primary reason for the share price decline.

claims.claim: American Express said second-quarter expenses increased 12% to $14.5 billion, compared with $12.9 billion a year ago.
claims.note: Livemint and other sources confirm American Express's Q2 expenses increased 12% to $14.5 billion, up from $12.9 billion a year ago.

article_title: American Express: Strong Revenue, Rising Costs & Investor Sentiment
